reason: negative side failed: preconditions accepted 1 of 15 unrelated states (diverged seed 0 resolves to 'merge'); a precondition set that accepts unrelated states is a defect. It also accepted 1 more state(s) it must refuse: preconditions accepted 1 of 1 same-intent states (lockfile_conflict seed 2 resolves to 'keep_local', which accepts ['keep_local']), and that is the state the program was compiled from: it declares variant 'take_upstream', but the solution it was compiled from is a 'keep_local' resolution there, so the declared variant, not the preconditions, is what is wrong

refused_program.intent: Update the current branch from upstream, merge the shared dependency file that both sides changed by keeping what the local side removed, and taking upstream's version of any single-valued line they both changed, then commit the merge.

postconditions.description: HEAD is a merge commit whose second parent is the upstream branch tip
postconditions.name: merge_commit_created

postconditions.description: every upstream commit is now reachable from HEAD
postconditions.name: upstream_is_ancestor

postconditions.description: the index has no unmerged entries and the working tree is clean
postconditions.name: no_unmerged_or_dirty_paths

postconditions.description: the shared file committed in HEAD carries no conflict markers
postconditions.name: no_conflict_markers
postconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD^1 HEAD^2) &&
f=$(comm -12 <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^1 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^2 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) | head -1) &&
test -n "$f" &&
! git show "HEAD:$f" | grep -q '^<<<<<<<'

postconditions.description: no line the local side had dropped from the merge base reappears in the merged file
postconditions.name: local_removals_still_removed
postconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD^1 HEAD^2) &&
f=$(comm -12 <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^1 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^2 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) | head -1) &&
test -n "$f" &&
! comm -23 <(git show "$base:$f" | sort -u) <(git show "HEAD^1:$f" | sort -u) | grep -qxF -f - <(git show "HEAD:$f")

postconditions.description: every line upstream added relative to the merge base is present in the merged file
postconditions.name: upstream_additions_present
postconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD^1 HEAD^2) &&
f=$(comm -12 <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^1 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD^2 | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) | head -1) &&
test -n "$f" &&
! comm -13 <(git show "$base:$f" | sort -u) <(git show "HEAD^2:$f" | sort -u) | grep -vxF -f <(git show "HEAD:$f") | grep -q .

preconditions.description: the upstream remote-tracking branch exists in this clone
preconditions.name: upstream_remote_ref_exists

preconditions.description: HEAD is a symbolically referenced branch, so the merge lands on a branch
preconditions.name: on_a_branch

preconditions.description: nothing is modified, staged or untracked in the working tree
preconditions.name: clean_worktree

preconditions.description: the repository is not already in the middle of a merge
preconditions.name: no_merge_in_progress

preconditions.description: local HEAD and the upstream branch each carry commits the other lacks, so a real merge is required
preconditions.name: branches_diverged

preconditions.description: exactly one path differs from the merge base on both sides, i.e. the two sides edited the same single file
preconditions.name: one_shared_file_changed
preconditions.probe:
base=$(git merge-base HEAD {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}) &&
test "$(comm -12 <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" HEAD | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) <(git diff --name-only -z "$base" {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch} | tr '\0' '\n' | sort) | grep -c .)" -eq 1
